title: Early directions gave no clear quadrant forecast gain within 200 km of 323 shallow M6.5+ centers in 2013-2024
abstract: We tested whether first-week event directions improve later location probabilities beyond older local directions. We used a fixed global ComCat M5.5+ snapshot. Centers had M6.5 or more and depth at most 70 km. Past-only isolation removed centers near an equal or larger recent event. We fit two smoothing weights with 363 centers in 2001-2012, then froze them. In 2013-2024, 323 centers supplied 219 event memberships on days 7-30 within 200 km. Adding quadrant counts from days 1-7 raised mean spatial log score by 0.01568 nats per target. The conditional 95% three-year block interval was -0.03056 to 0.07376. This gives no clear forecast gain. A 300 km check gave a positive interval before adjustment for multiple checks; the other four checks did not. This tests coarse spatial persistence, conditional on event count. It does not test physical migration or operational forecasts. Few targets, shared memberships, revised mixed-network records, fixed quadrants and conditional uncertainty limit inference. Code, source hashes, aggregate scores, simulations, a figure and a separate scalar audit are included. Source records remain external.

display.caption: Added spatial log scores for all planned tests and primary annual scores. Intervals hold fitted weights fixed and resample three-year blocks. Positive scores favor early directions.

citations.reason: Provides center and window design for a count-distribution test. Our source and samples overlap.
Mean early distance was already tested for later count skill. We instead test directional allocation.
Prior two-sequence quadrant trend test motivates a global test of constant early directions against older local directions.
Exact external snapshot identified by path and SHA-256 in files/provenance.json.
